scenario.description: A pottery-kiln owner must decide whether to accept a neighbor's batch-firing job and settle the exact price, firing schedule, pickup arrangement, and glaze-safety terms after checking the proposal with the people gathered at the shared studio.

agents.name: June
agents.role: Another Ceramicist with a Competing Offer

shared_context.S1: Elena has an electric pottery kiln available for informal jobs at the shared studio.
shared_context.S2: Marcus is interested in having a batch of pottery fired by Elena.
shared_context.S3: The kiln is normally booked by verbal agreement, with the owner deciding the final terms.
shared_context.S4: Before Elena closes an arrangement, the studio's usual check-in is for each person present to state any relevant terms, constraints, or safety requirements.

PF1.text: Marcus's proposal is for 24 mugs, for a total price of exactly $90, with bisque firing on Tuesday evening, glaze firing on Saturday morning, and pickup on Sunday at 12:00.

PF2.text: June has another customer willing to pay exactly $120 cash for the same Saturday glaze-firing slot, so Elena has a concrete cash alternative to compare with Marcus's job.

PF3.text: Ravi measured the kiln shelves and confirmed that 24 mugs require two separate bisque loads; one bisque load would not safely fit all 24 mugs, while the Saturday glaze load can fit them together.

PF4.text: Sofia learned from the restaurant manager receiving Marcus's mugs that all 24 are intended for food service and must be fired with lead-free, food-safe glaze; this requirement has not yet been shared with Elena.

acceptance_conditions: Elena must accept Marcus's job for exactly 24 mugs at a total price of $90.
The firing plan must include two separate bisque loads before one Saturday glaze load.
Pickup must be set for Sunday at 12:00.
The settlement must record the $120 cash alternative for the same glaze-firing slot.
The settlement must require lead-free, food-safe glaze for all 24 mugs.
The settlement must explicitly record two bisque firings and one glaze firing.
The settlement must explicitly confirm that two bisque loads are required.
The settlement must explicitly confirm lead-free glaze.
Elena must cite the food-service requirement when justifying the glaze-safety term.

decisive_facts.why: Marcus's exact proposal changes the client to Marcus, the mug count to exactly 24, the price to exactly $90, and the pickup terms to Sunday at 12:00.
June's competing offer changes the recorded comparison from no benchmark to exactly $120 cash for the same Saturday glaze-firing slot.
Ravi's shelf measurement changes the firing counts to exactly two bisque firings and one glaze firing and changes the capacity confirmation to two required bisque loads.
Sofia's food-service requirement changes the glaze decisions to required food-safe and lead-free glaze for all 24 mugs and supplies the fact Elena must cite.
